days.title: Arrival, Free Tour Setup & City Wander

timeBlocks.name: afternoon
timeBlocks.description: Arrival via Ryanair FR9601 at Madrid (MAD) 11:35, transfer to Onefam Madrid (central Madrid, Centro neighborhood), check in and ask reception about the free walking tour.

activities.name: Arrival at Madrid (MAD) & Transfer to Hostel
activities.notes: Arrive via Ryanair FR9601 from Rome Fiumicino. Metro Line 8 from the airport to Nuevos Ministerios, then connect toward Conde Duque/Argüelles (~35-45 min total), or taxi directly to Montserrat, 9.

activities.name: Check-in at Onefam Madrid & Ask About the Free Tour
activities.notes: Check in, settle into the room, and ask reception for the exact day/time of the hostel's free walking tour - sign up on the spot if there's a slot available. With an 11:35 arrival, there's a gap before the 15:00 check-in - ask about early luggage storage.

timeBlocks.name: evening
timeBlocks.description: Free Tour of the hostel and wander through central Madrid - grouped together since the exact tour time is unknown, similar to the London/Vienna approach.

activities.name: Free Tour of the Hostel ⭐
activities.suggestedTime: ⚠️ Time TBD - confirm exact schedule at reception
activities.timeRestriction: ⚠️ NOT CONFIRMED - exact day/time unknown until asked at check-in
activities.notes: Hostel-organized free walking tour - Onefam Madrid (Montserrat, 9) is in the Conde Duque/Argüelles area, a short walk/metro ride from Centro, so the tour likely covers Gran Vía, Sol, and the surrounding historic core.

bookingDetails.advanceTimeNeeded: Confirm and sign up in person at reception on arrival

activities.name: Wander Through Central Madrid (Sol, Gran Vía, Plaza Mayor)
activities.notes: Casual first-night stroll through Puerta del Sol, Gran Vía (Madrid's 'Broadway', lit up at night), and Plaza Mayor - all within easy walking distance of the hostel. Great for getting oriented before tomorrow's shopping day.

activities.name: Dinner (Flexible)
activities.notes: Tapas dinner somewhere around Centro/La Latina - pick based on wherever the tour/wander ends up.

research_notes.notes: Day 1 kept light and flexible, mirroring the London/Vienna approach: arrive, check in, ask reception about the free tour's actual schedule, then fit in a casual wander through central Madrid around it. Full shopping day saved for Day 2.

days.title: Full Shopping Day - Cheap, Good Quality Clothes

timeBlocks.name: morning
timeBlocks.description: Early start at Gran Vía and Fuencarral - Madrid's main shopping corridors, good mix of affordable chains and quality finds.

activities.name: Gran Vía Shopping ⭐
activities.notes: Madrid's main shopping avenue - Zara, Primark, H&M, Mango, Bershka, and other Spanish/European chains known for decent quality at low prices. Start early to beat the crowds.

activities.name: Calle de Fuencarral
activities.notes: Trendy pedestrian shopping street north of Gran Vía (Malasaña/Chueca area) - mix of streetwear brands, independent boutiques, and more affordable alternative fashion than the touristy core.

timeBlocks.name: lunch
timeBlocks.description: Lunch break around Malasaña or Chueca before continuing to the outlet/market area.

activities.name: Lunch in Malasaña/Chueca
activities.notes: Quick lunch break (menú del día is a great cheap option, usually 10-15 EUR for 2-3 courses) before continuing shopping.

timeBlocks.name: afternoon
timeBlocks.description: Continue shopping - secondhand/vintage options for good quality at lower prices, plus El Corte Inglés for a one-stop department store option.

activities.name: El Corte Inglés (Callao/Preciados)
activities.notes: Spain's major department store chain - wider range of brands and quality levels under one roof, useful if a specific item is proving hard to find on the street shops. Can be pricier than the chain stores, but good for quality basics/outerwear on sale.

activities.name: Mercado de Fuencarral / Vintage & Secondhand Shops
activities.notes: Alternative/vintage indoor market with secondhand and independent streetwear stalls - good source of unique, well-made pieces at lower prices than retail. Malasaña also has several standalone vintage/thrift shops worth a browse.

activities.name: Primark Gran Vía (Flagship Store)
activities.notes: One of the largest Primark stores in Europe, housed in a historic building on Gran Vía - extremely cheap basics, worth a stop if hunting for budget essentials.

timeBlocks.name: evening
timeBlocks.description: Wind down with dinner and pack purchases before the early flight the next morning.

activities.name: Dinner & Pack for Early Departure
activities.notes: Relaxed dinner back near the hostel, then pack everything (including new clothes) that night since the flight home departs early at 10:25 the next morning.

research_notes.notes: Full day dedicated to shopping as requested - starts early (09:00) at Gran Vía/Fuencarral for the main chain stores, then El Corte Inglés and vintage/secondhand options in the afternoon for better quality finds at lower prices, with Primark as an optional cheap-basics stop. Pack new purchases the night before given the early 10:25 flight on Day 3.

timeBlocks.name: morning
timeBlocks.description: Early checkout and transfer to Madrid Barajas Airport for the confirmed 10:25 flight home.

activities.name: Check Out & Transfer to Madrid Barajas (MAD)
activities.timeRestriction: Checkout officially 11:00, but must leave much earlier for the flight
activities.notes: Metro Line 8 from Nuevos Ministerios (or a taxi) to the airport, ~30-40 min depending on terminal. Pack the night before since you'll be leaving well before normal checkout time.

must_try_dishes.description: Madrid's iconic street food - crispy fried squid rings in a baguette, a Plaza Mayor classic.
Hearty chickpea stew with meats and vegetables, traditionally served in courses (soup, then chickpeas/veg, then meats).
must_try_dishes.seasonal: Especially popular in colder months (good timing for November)

must_try_dishes.description: Thick potato and egg omelette, served as a tapa or full plate, found everywhere from bars to markets.
Fried dough sticks dipped in thick hot chocolate - classic breakfast or late-night snack, famously at Chocolatería San Ginés.
Fixed-price lunch menu (starter + main + dessert/coffee + drink), common at local restaurants on weekdays - great value.

drinks_and_rituals.description: The standard small beer pour in Madrid, often comes with a free tapa at traditional bars.
Pre-lunch aperitif tradition, often on draft ('de grifo'), served with olives.

restaurants.name: Mercado de San Miguel
restaurants.notes: Historic iron-and-glass market turned gourmet food hall - touristy but a great variety of small bites in one place, very close to the hostel.

restaurants.name: Chocolatería San Ginés
restaurants.notes: Madrid institution open 24 hours since 1894 - famous for the best churros con chocolate in the city.

restaurants.name: Casa Labra
restaurants.notes: Historic tapas bar since 1860, famous for its fried cod tapas - cheap, authentic, and steps from Puerta del Sol.

special_meal_formats: Menú del día - fixed-price weekday lunch deal, one of the best value meals in Madrid (10-15 EUR for 2-3 courses + drink)
tourist_traps_to_avoid: Restaurants directly on Plaza Mayor - inflated prices for mediocre food; walk a block or two away for much better value
Overpriced sangria pitchers marketed to tourists near major landmarks - ask locals or check reviews before ordering

average_food_budget_reference.note: Rough daily food budget guide for Madrid (per person)

ticket_types: 10-trip Metrobús ticket - ~12.20 EUR (shareable, good value for short stays)

where_to_buy.machines: Ticket machines at any Metro station, cash or card

practical_tips: ✅ All of Madrid is now fully confirmed: accommodation (Onefam Madrid), arrival flight (Ryanair FR9601), and departure flight (World2Fly 2W2075). Non-refundable rate - paying by card at the property incurs a 4% surcharge, consider cash.
Shopping day: Gran Vía and Fuencarral open around 10:00 - arriving right at opening maximizes time before afternoon crowds.
The departure flight (10:25) is early relative to the 11:00 checkout - pack the night before Day 2 ends.
El Corte Inglés and Primark both accept tax-free shopping refunds for non-EU residents - keep receipts if buying higher-value items.

research_notes.notes: Built around the confirmed Ryanair FR9601 arrival (Rome FCO → Madrid, Nov 10), the confirmed Onefam Madrid accommodation (Montserrat, 9, booking 3856344534112), and the confirmed World2Fly return flight (Madrid→Rosario, Nov 12). Day 1 is arrival + free tour + city wander; Day 2 is a full dedicated shopping day for cheap, good-quality clothes (Gran Vía, Fuencarral, vintage/secondhand, El Corte Inglés, Primark); Day 3 is the confirmed departure. Madrid is now 100% confirmed - accommodation, arrival, and departure.
